page: Microsoft Azure D4ps_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dpsv6 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated physical ARM64 cores powered by a Microsoft ARM Neoverse-N2 processor operating at 3.4 GHz. The CPU configuration includes a single thread per core, 64 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 128 MB of L3 cache. The system is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include any onboard GPUs or local storage, though it is Premium Storage capable for external disk attachments.

Performance benchmarks place the D4ps_v6 in the average tier for most general computing tasks. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests yield average results, as do the Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores. Notably, single-threaded gzip compression performance is strong, placing in the top 25% of tested systems, and PassMark memory performance is similarly strong. However, the ARM64 architecture lacks advanced vector and matrix extensions, resulting in weak performance in ray tracing, image processing, and LLM prompt processing. PassMark CPU encryption tests also register in the bottom 10%, reflecting a lack of specialized hardware acceleration for certain cryptographic operations beyond standard AES.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D4ps_v6 offers a resource-dense ARM-based profile that delivers steady, predictable performance for workloads that do not rely on x86-specific instruction sets. Given its balanced memory-to-CPU ratio and average database and web serving benchmarks, this server is appropriate for general-purpose workloads such as static web serving, application hosting, software compilation, and basic database operations.
